articleBody:
A smooth walk-in shower remodel starts with good preparation before tools arrive. Run through this checklist to keep your home organized and avoid delays:

- [ ] Clear personal items from the bathroom — Empty all medicine cabinets, vanity drawers, and open shelving so technicians have immediate, safe room to work.
- [ ] Establish a secondary bathing routine — Set up schedules for using a spare bath or guest suite, especially during the plumbing and tile curing phases.
- [ ] Measure hallway and doorway clearances — Check access paths between your entry door and the bathroom so materials, tile boxes, and shower pans move through easily.
- [ ] Finalize your plumbing fixture layout — Confirm the placement of your main showerhead, handheld sprayer, and valve heights before wall boards are installed.
- [ ] Mark locations for grab bar reinforcement — Identify where you want solid wood blocking added inside the walls to support current or future safety rails.
- [ ] Select slip-resistant floor surfaces — Pick mosaic or textured floor tiles that offer dependable grip under soapy, wet conditions.
- [ ] Protect path floors and adjacent rooms — Lay down drop cloths and close bedroom doors along the primary pathway to contain dust from demolition.
- [ ] Review the written contractor scope — Double-check that your quote explicitly lists demolition, disposal, licensed plumbing, and waterproofing systems.

### How to Use This Checklist
Walk through these items a week before work starts. Getting details settled early prevents work pauses once demolition begins.
